evidence: The user's interview answer 7 for the coordination-shells skill (question 7 of section 2 in docs/SKILL_INTERVIEWS.md): corner-sharing or extended networks of polyhedra are judged by angle spreads plus a standard polyhedral distortion index, never by the cluster null. No tool measured a polyhedron's distortion: analyze_clusters' shuffle null needs finite clusters of one element and reports an extended network instead (the TiO6 of a perovskite, the tetrahedra of a spinel), and compute_bond_angles gives the angle distribution of a triplet but no per-polyhedron index, nor the average structure's polyhedron to tell a static distortion from thermal spread. dev-jahn-teller is the case in point: every CuF6 is 4 x 1.93 + 2 x 2.25 A, its long axis drawn per cell, so the average octahedron is regular and the distortion is local only. The tool as built: Baur's bond-length distortion index DI = (1/n) sum |l_i - <l>|/<l> (Acta Cryst. B30 (1974) 1195) and, for octahedra and tetrahedra, Robinson's quadratic elongation <lambda> = (1/n) sum (l_i/l0)^2 (l0 of the regular polyhedron of the same volume) and bond-angle variance sigma^2 = sum (theta_i - theta0)^2/(m - 1) over Robinson's cis angles (12 of an octahedron, the 15 less the trans matching with the largest angle sum, theta0 = 90 deg; the 6 of a tetrahedron, theta0 = arccos(-1/3)) (Science 172 (1971) 567), over the configuration's polyhedra of the most common count (the triplets engine's neighbour search) and over the average structure's (the structure_basis site means). Known answers: regular octahedron and tetrahedron 0, 1, 0; the 4 + 2 octahedron at 1.93/2.25 A DI = (4|1.93 - <l>| + 2|2.25 - <l>|)/(6<l>) = 0.069831 with <l> = 2.03667, <lambda> = 1.010845 in closed form, sigma^2 = 0; a trigonal octahedron sigma^2 = 12 delta^2/11 (51.61 deg^2 at psi = 50 deg); a flattened tetrahedron and an off-centred atom (<lambda> = 1 + (delta/R)^2) in closed form; a thermal-only corner-sharing network (1,000 TiO6, the O displaced 0.05 A per axis and centred per site) whose mean DI is sqrt(2/pi) sqrt(5/6) s/<l> (0.01862 against 0.01880) and sigma^2 (24/11)(s/<l>)^2 (180/pi)^2 (4.74 against 4.71 deg^2) within four standard errors plus 1 % and 2 %, and whose average octahedron is regular (DI 2e-17); orientationally disordered JT octahedra with DI 0.069831 each and a regular average. The browser port matches the golden to 1e-9, refusals' messages included. On the Demo the TaSe6 octahedra read DI 0.0469 +/- 0.017, <lambda> 1.0405, sigma^2 127 deg^2 against the average structure's 0.0415, 1.0341 and 111 deg^2 (bonds 3 x 2.52 + 3 x 2.75 A: a static distortion), the GaSe4 tetrahedra DI 0.0278 against 0.0010 (thermal only); on dev-jahn-teller the CuF6 configuration DI exceeds 0.0698 while the average octahedron's is below a tenth of it. Arms A and A+ on dev before and after: all 45 records identical but for protocol and commit (A+ does not read the tool). The held-out test set was not run. What the model sees: the tool's definition in the dock (+1,745 characters) and arms B (+1,741) and C (+1,246: its description without the method advice), the first-request tool lists and a new tool-results sample; the 48k worst turns keep 7,041 (dock) and 9,776 (arm B) tokens with the batch-1 skill drafts (9,746 and 12,480 before them). proposed_fix: A new engine, rmc_toolkits/distortion.py polyhedral_distortion(config, centre, ligand, r_min, r_max, max_bonds) (source of truth, exported from rmc_toolkits), and its straight port workers/distortion.js polyhedralDistortion over triplets.js's exported neighborBonds: the coordination histogram and coordinationSummary, the polyhedra of the most common count n among centres with a ligand (the lowest on a tie), the rest counted; per polyhedron DI, and for n = 6 or 4 <lambda>, sigma^2_theta and (octahedra) the mean trans angle, each summarised as {count, mean, sd, p10, median, p90} over the configuration and over the average structure (a site counting as its majority species; per-site rows; reason no_basis, no_centre_sites or coordination_differs). The PCA worker's 'distortion' request (the basis from structureFromRmc6f, cached per text), ANALYSIS_ROUTES and /api/distortion (_number validation, rMax <= 8 A, APP_MAX_BONDS = 1e6 bonds counted before any is stored, _FileCache keyed on every engine argument, strict JSON); the request contract gains the route, its limits and 17 cases; REFERENCE.md its row. The Copilot tool polyhedral_distortion(centre, ligand, r_min, r_max, window_confirmed?) (summarizePolyhedra, a dataShape, no facts) refuses a window that cuts the shell by compute_bond_angles' rule (shells.js windowCut through its one shellWindows entry: the CN margin against the run's shell, the engine's counts where there is none) unless window_confirmed, keeping the counts and the shell reading; on every natural window of the Demo it refuses exactly where compute_bond_angles refuses and the Workbench asks. Its description states only what it computes (arm C); its method field adds the window's source, which questions need it and the static/local reading (dock, arm B). Protocol 2026-10-24.3. Commits d6b86b5 (engines, route, worker, golden), d6435bb (tool), 1e36011. Not done here (other PRs own the files): the verification's claim catalogue still backs a 'distorted octahedra' conclusion with analyze_clusters only, and the coordination-shells skill does not name the tool.
